title: Economic conditions

match.reason: The closest bank point, bus-economic-financial-influences, is broader than the new point because it also covers inflation and exchange rates, and it leaves out tax rates and consumer confidence, so it is related rather than the same idea.

draft.title: Economic conditions
card: Economic conditions are the state of the wider economy. A business cannot control them, but they shape how much customers spend and what it costs to run.
the cost of borrowing money. When rates rise, loan repayments rise, so a business pays more to borrow and many households have less left to spend.
when more people have jobs, more households have income to spend. Higher tax rates take more from income and profit, which can reduce spending and the money a business keeps.
how secure people feel about their money and jobs. When confidence is low, customers tend to delay big purchases and spend less, even if their income has not changed.
draft.remember: Economic conditions change what customers can spend, what they are willing to spend, and what it costs a business to borrow.

a.q: Interest rates rise across Australia. How could this affect a new café owner who has a bank loan?
opts: Loan repayments rise, and customers may spend less
Loan repayments fall, and customers may spend more
Loan repayments rise, and customers may spend more
Loan repayments stay the same, and customers spend less
a.why: Higher rates make borrowing cost more, so repayments on the loan rise. Households with loans also have less left to spend. Lower repayments would only follow a fall in rates, not a rise.
a.clue: Think about what a higher cost of borrowing does to both the owner and customers.

b.q: Priya sells prams from a shop in Geelong. Jobs are plentiful, but a news report makes many families worried about their finances. Which result is most likely?
opts: Families delay buying prams, so her sales may fall
Families buy more prams, because jobs are plentiful
Her sales are unaffected, because incomes have not changed
Her loan costs fall, because families are worried
b.why: Low consumer confidence makes people put off big purchases, even when jobs are plentiful. Plentiful jobs alone would suggest more spending, which is the tempting wrong answer. Worry about finances can still hold spending back.
b.clue: Confidence is about how people feel, not only about their income.

a.best: Loan repayments rise, and customers may spend less

b.best: Families delay buying prams, so her sales may fall
